proof.text: Reduction to the residue field defines a homomorphism of root groups. A root reducing to 1 has a geometric sum with residue n, hence a unit. Multiply it by the difference from 1 to get zero, and cancel the unit; the kernel is trivial.

Lift each residue root by the simple-root condition HenselianLocalRing.TFAE, using the derivative n times the root to the (n-1)th power. The resulting element has nth power 1, so construct its inverse as the (n-1)th power. This proves surjectivity without choosing any algebra data.

Use the equivalence of root groups to transfer cardinality n from HasEnoughRootsOfUnity.natCard_rootsOfUnity. Transfer cyclicity along the injective homomorphism. For a nonidentity root, the injective reduction cannot be 1, so its difference from 1 has nonzero residue and is a unit.

title: Roots of unity in a strict local ring
statement: Let $H$ be a strictly henselian local commutative ring (henselian local in [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] with separably closed residue field), and let $n>0$ have $n$ a unit in $H$. Put $\mu_n(H)=\{\zeta\in H^\times:\zeta^n=1\}$. Then $\mu_n(H)$ has cardinality $n$ and is cyclic. Moreover, for every nonidentity $\zeta\in\mu_n(H)$ the element $\zeta-1$ is a unit in $H$.

lean.statement:
theorem strict_local_roots_of_unity
    (H : Type u) [CommRing H] [IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing H]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n ∧ IsUnit (n : H)) :
    Nat.card (rootsOfUnity n H) = n ∧ IsCyclic (rootsOfUnity n H) ∧
      ∀ ζ : rootsOfUnity n H, ζ ≠ 1 → IsUnit (((ζ : Hˣ) : H) - 1)
